title.narrative: Accelerating Energy Efficiency in Cambodia’s Building Sector

description.narrative: This Joint Program (JP) aims to support Cambodia’s latest Updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) to reduce 41% of domestic greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 compared to business as usual, concentrated primarily in the Forest and Land Use, energy, agriculture, industry, and waste sectors. Accordingly, a general national goal to reduce total energy consumption was set at 19% by 2030, with a 25% reduction in the building sector in particular. As such, the JP aims to accelerate Energy Efficiency (EE) to achieve Cambodia’s development ambitions for sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth and its national climate action agenda, including the NDCs. In doing so, the project focuses on three drivers of change following a whole-of-society approach. It addresses behavioural, market, and regulatory barriers to EE. It will step up advocacy for EE policy, practices, and finance. In aggregate, the JP helps strengthen the ecosystem for EE and lays a foundation for EE at scale. The analytical work of the JP will inform the formulation of the NDC3.0. The JP serves as a platform for convening multi-stakeholder participation, partnership, and collaboration. It brings together key players in the EE ecosystem for policy dialogue, identifying and co-designing solutions, and developing partnerships for sustaining acceleration beyond the implementation of this JP. The JP will accelerate ongoing work and advocacy for integrating energy efficiency design guidelines (Building Energy Code), supporting the Building Technical Regulations and ensuring policy alignment. The JP will also support selected commercial and public buildings for the implementation of EE measures by facilitating mainly access to finance and availing potential market and fiscal incentives.
